note: Hebrew shibbolim are ears of grain (wheat or barley); "corn" in 1611 meant any cereal, but modern (especially American) readers hear maize, unknown in the ancient Near East. Recurs with bar/shever ("corn") through chs. 41-47.
Hebrew 'avrek is an obscure, probably Egyptian or Akkadian, word (perhaps "Attention!" or a title); "Bow the knee" rests on a folk derivation from Hebrew barak "kneel".
